## Constellation Graph

### Layout — No Separate Page
- There is no dedicated graph view page; the standalone route was removed entirely
- The constellation lives inside the **sidebar** (left/right dock) as a live vis-network instance
- A full-screen **overlay** is available via the MAP button, with a floating legend card and a scale-out open animation

### Sidebar Graph Behavior
- Sidebar graph uses smaller nodes (size range 28–44)
- Physics engine freezes after initial stabilization to keep the layout stable during interaction
- **Node emphasis:** the current node and its immediate neighbors render at full opacity; all other nodes fade to 30%

### Pan & Stabilization
- **Bounded panning:** a custom pointer-based pan handler clamps movement to the node bounding box, preventing the user from scrolling into empty space
- **Stabilization settings:** 150 iterations with `updateInterval: 150` — the graph renders once after settling rather than animating every intermediate frame

### Shared Infrastructure
- `createGraphNetwork()` factory in `src/engine/createGraphNetwork.ts` is shared by both the sidebar instance and the overlay instance

Created: Apr 4, 2026 · Updated: Apr 10, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

Content from GitHub API

Data Sources

  • Fetches issues, README, and the full file tree from the GitHub API
  • PRs and commits are not fetched — removed due to unreliable linking between PR nodes and the rest of the graph

File Tree Processing

  • Generates a repo-root node, directory nodes (2 levels deep), and individual source file nodes for .ts, .tsx, .md, .json, .yaml, and .css files
  • Each file node is parented to its containing directory node

README Handling

  • README content is decoded with TextDecoder instead of atob to fix UTF-8 encoding issues with base64 content
  • Content-based connections are created via keyword matching: a connection forms when 60% or more of a target node's title words appear in the README body
  • #N issue references in the README also generate explicit connections

Issue Processing

  • Issues with 2 or more headings are split into a parent node plus individual section nodes

Caching & Error Handling

  • CACHE_VERSION constant enables cache versioning; stale data is auto-cleared on version bump
  • An error screen is displayed when 0 nodes load (typically due to API rate limiting)

Hub Node Selection

  • The hub node (center of the graph) prefers the readme node; falls back to the highest-degree node

## Content from GitHub API

### Data Sources
- Fetches **issues**, **README**, and the **full file tree** from the GitHub API
- PRs and commits are **not** fetched — removed due to unreliable linking between PR nodes and the rest of the graph

### File Tree Processing
- Generates a **repo-root** node, **directory** nodes (2 levels deep), and individual **source file** nodes for `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.md`, `.json`, `.yaml`, and `.css` files
- Each file node is parented to its containing directory node

### README Handling
- README content is decoded with `TextDecoder` instead of `atob` to fix UTF-8 encoding issues with base64 content
- Content-based connections are created via keyword matching: a connection forms when 60% or more of a target node's title words appear in the README body
- `#N` issue references in the README also generate explicit connections

### Issue Processing
- Issues with 2 or more headings are split into a **parent** node plus individual **section** nodes

### Caching & Error Handling
- `CACHE_VERSION` constant enables cache versioning; stale data is auto-cleared on version bump
- An error screen is displayed when 0 nodes load (typically due to API rate limiting)

### Hub Node Selection
- The hub node (center of the graph) prefers the `readme` node; falls back to the highest-degree node

Created: Apr 4, 2026 · Updated: Apr 5, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

Vision

Phase 2 introduces an embedded GitHub Copilot conversation panel directly inside kbexplorer. Users will be able to ask questions about the knowledge base — "What issues are related to authentication?", "Summarize the architecture decisions", "What's blocking the next release?" — and receive contextual answers grounded in the loaded graph data.

How It Would Work

  1. A collapsible chat panel slides in from the right side of the reading view, hosted inside a Fluent Dialog component for consistent overlay behavior
  2. The conversation context includes the current node's content, its connections, and the full graph structure
  3. Copilot generates responses using the knowledge graph as grounding — not generic answers, but answers specific to this repository's issues and structure
  4. Responses can include clickable node references that navigate within kbexplorer

Integration Points

  • The HUD (#11) would gain a chat toggle Fluent Button in the right panel
  • The graph view (#10) could support "find nodes about X" queries that highlight matching nodes
  • The reading view would show inline suggestions for related content based on what you're reading
  • The overview could offer a "summarize this cluster" action per cluster group
  • All conversation UI would use Fluent components (Card, Button, Input, Body1, etc.) to match the existing design system

Technical Approach

This would use the GitHub Copilot Extensions SDK to embed a Copilot-powered experience. The knowledge graph (#12) provides structured context that makes responses significantly more relevant than raw repository search. The Fluent theme system (#13) would style the chat panel automatically through FluentProvider context.

This is a Phase 2 feature — the current Phase 1 focuses on making the exploration experience excellent on its own (#9, #10, #11).

nodes.title: Epic: Open, data-driven node-type engine for kbexplorer-template

nodes.content: We adopt the proven three-layer model from content-model.md: identity (teamops.yaml → kg:// URN authority/org) → shape (schema/conventions.yaml, edges.yaml, lifecycle.yaml, entities/*.schema.json, index/context.jsonld) → content (one file per entity). URN = JSON-LD @id; kind = @type (never inferred from path); edges.yaml is the relationship manifest; a 5-pass builder walks files → resolves edges → derives → clusters → stubs unresolved targets.
nodes.rawContent: We adopt the proven three-layer model from `content-model.md`: **identity** (`teamops.yaml` → `kg://` URN authority/org) → **shape** (`schema/conventions.yaml`, `edges.yaml`, `lifecycle.yaml`, `entities/*.schema.json`, `index/context.jsonld`) → **content** (one file per entity). URN = JSON-LD `@id`; kind = `@type` (never inferred from path); `edges.yaml` is the relationship manifest; a 5-pass builder walks files → resolves edges → derives → clusters → stubs unresolved targets.

nodes.title: Scope boundaries

nodes.content: On real content, a Person node and a Squad node render via bespoke viewers, an arbitrary structured file renders via the generic fallback, and a .github workflow appears as a node edged to the repository node — all without editing core unions to introduce a new kind.
nodes.rawContent: On **real content**, a Person node and a Squad node render via bespoke viewers, an arbitrary structured file renders via the generic fallback, and a `.github` workflow appears as a node edged to the repository node — all **without editing core unions** to introduce a new kind.
nodes.title: Success definition

nodes.content:
Replace kbexplorer-template's closed, compile-time node-type system — hardcoded NodeSource / DisplayMode / EdgeType unions, a renderContent switch, and bespoke per-source providers — with an open, data-driven one:

  • JSON-LD node internals (@id / @type / typed data) on KBNode.
  • A node-type registry that declares each type's discovery, mapping, cluster, layer, relations, and viewer in one place.
  • A viewer registry keyed by @type with a generic structured fallback (total coverage; bespoke viewers are additive).
  • Schema-driven content-model ingestion that builds the graph from entity files (the model documented in content-model.md).
  • Repo-structural discovery: .github workflows, Actions, and templates become nodes linked to the repository node.
nodes.rawContent:
Replace kbexplorer-template's **closed, compile-time** node-type system — hardcoded `NodeSource` / `DisplayMode` / `EdgeType` unions, a `renderContent` switch, and bespoke per-source providers — with an **open, data-driven** one:

- **JSON-LD node internals** (`@id` / `@type` / typed `data`) on `KBNode`.
- A **node-type registry** that declares each type's discovery, mapping, cluster, layer, relations, and viewer in one place.
- A **viewer registry keyed by `@type`** with a generic structured fallback (total coverage; bespoke viewers are additive).
- **Schema-driven content-model ingestion** that builds the graph from entity files (the model documented in `content-model.md`).
- **Repo-structural discovery**: `.github` workflows, Actions, and templates become nodes linked to the repository node.
nodes.title: What

nodes.content: The originating content-model repo (Xbox Personalization) is being sunset. kbexplorer-template must become the new system of record and own the files→graph pipeline itself — no dependency on an externally pre-built graph.json. Migration will surface new node kinds (squad/cell/crew, sprint/cycle/season, …) that must be absorbed by configuration, not core surgery. Repo structure should be first-class graph citizens. JSON-LD + a viewer registry is the smallest durable abstraction that delivers the originally requested Person / Squad / Team views and scales to arbitrary structured knowledge.
nodes.rawContent: The originating content-model repo (Xbox Personalization) is being **sunset**. kbexplorer-template must become the new system of record and **own the files→graph pipeline itself** — no dependency on an externally pre-built `graph.json`. JSON-LD + a viewer registry is the smallest durable abstraction that delivers the originally requested Person / Squad / Team views *and* scales to arbitrary structured knowledge.

Overview

While the default experience uses GitHub API data (#12), kbexplorer also supports an authored mode where content comes from a collection of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. This mode is designed for curated knowledge bases — design systems, architecture decision records, learning curricula, or team wikis.

Frontmatter Schema

Each .md file declares its metadata in YAML frontmatter:

`yaml

title: Authentication Architecture cluster: security emoji: 🔐 sprite: /images/auth-icon.png hero: /images/auth-hero.jpg connections:

  • id: session-management type: references
  • id: oauth-flow type: depends-on tags: [architecture, security, phase-1]

`

The engine parses these files using gray-matter, builds the graph from explicit connections arrays, and assigns visuals based on the mode selected (#9).

Rendering

All prose is rendered using Fluent tokens for typography and colors. The default font is Segoe UI (via tokens.fontFamilyBase) for body text and headings. Code blocks use Cascadia Code (via tokens.fontFamilyMonospace). Colors, spacing, and radii all come from Fluent tokens through makeStyles — no custom CSS variables or hardcoded values.

Clustering

In authored mode, clusters come from the cluster field rather than GitHub labels. This gives authors explicit control over how nodes group in the overview grid and the constellation graph (#10). The same cluster colors and visual indicators carry through the HUD (#11) and reading view connections sidebar.

When to Use Which Mode

  • Repo-aware (default): Zero-config exploration of any GitHub repo. Great for project onboarding. PRs are filtered out — only issues, README, and directory structure become nodes.
  • Authored: Curated, designed knowledge experiences. Requires content creation but offers full control over structure, visuals, and narrative flow.

## Overview

While the default experience uses GitHub API data (#12), kbexplorer also supports an **authored mode** where content comes from a collection of Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. This mode is designed for curated knowledge bases — design systems, architecture decision records, learning curricula, or team wikis.

### Frontmatter Schema

Each `.md` file declares its metadata in YAML frontmatter:

`yaml
---
title: Authentication Architecture
cluster: security
emoji: 🔐
sprite: /images/auth-icon.png
hero: /images/auth-hero.jpg
connections:
  - id: session-management
    type: references
  - id: oauth-flow
    type: depends-on
tags: [architecture, security, phase-1]
---
`

The engine parses these files using `gray-matter`, builds the graph from explicit `connections` arrays, and assigns visuals based on the mode selected (#9).

### Rendering

All prose is rendered using Fluent tokens for typography and colors. The default font is **Segoe UI** (via `tokens.fontFamilyBase`) for body text and headings. Code blocks use **Cascadia Code** (via `tokens.fontFamilyMonospace`). Colors, spacing, and radii all come from Fluent tokens through `makeStyles` — no custom CSS variables or hardcoded values.

### Clustering

In authored mode, clusters come from the `cluster` field rather than GitHub labels. This gives authors explicit control over how nodes group in the overview grid and the constellation graph (#10). The same cluster colors and visual indicators carry through the HUD (#11) and reading view connections sidebar.

### When to Use Which Mode

- **Repo-aware** (default): Zero-config exploration of any GitHub repo. Great for project onboarding. PRs are filtered out — only issues, README, and directory structure become nodes.
- **Authored**: Curated, designed knowledge experiences. Requires content creation but offers full control over structure, visuals, and narrative flow.

nodes.title: Epic: External theme & branding customization (no submodule edits)

nodes.content:
• Transport: config.yaml theme: (Option A) is the backbone; dedicated theme files (B), raw CSS (C) and JS module (D) are later substitutes/escape hatches.
  • Scope axis: global → per-cluster → per-page, always as TOKEN DELTAS layered on the active base theme (dark/light/sepia) — never a full theme replacement, so the global theme switcher keeps working.
  • Assets (logos/favicons) are orthogonal URL refs resolved through the existing resolveImageUrl(source, …) host-repo path.
  • Start simple and grow: 5 phases, each shippable independently.
nodes.rawContent:
- Transport: `config.yaml theme:` (Option A) is the backbone; dedicated theme
  files (B), raw CSS (C) and JS module (D) are later substitutes/escape hatches.
- Scope axis: global → per-cluster → per-page, always as TOKEN DELTAS layered on
  the active base theme (dark/light/sepia) — never a full theme replacement, so
  the global theme switcher keeps working.
- Assets (logos/favicons) are orthogonal URL refs resolved through the existing
  `resolveImageUrl(source, …)` host-repo path.
- Start simple and grow: 5 phases, each shippable independently.

nodes.title: scripts/generate-manifest.js ignores VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT in vendored installs

nodes.content:
detectHostRoot() resolves kbRoot/../.., which only works for git-submodule layouts (where .kbexplorer is two levels deep). In vendored mode that path lands above the host repo, the lookup fails, and the script falls back to treating kbRoot as the host.

The companion CLI (anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli) already passes VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT=<host> via env on dev/build, but this script never reads it.
nodes.rawContent:
`detectHostRoot()` resolves `kbRoot/../..`, which only works for git-submodule layouts (where `.kbexplorer` is two levels deep). In vendored mode that path lands **above** the host repo, the lookup fails, and the script falls back to treating `kbRoot` as the host.

The companion CLI (`anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli`) already passes `VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT=<host>` via env on dev/build, but this script never reads it.
nodes.title: Cause

nodes.content: Until this is fixed, kbexplorer dev in a vendored install renders the template's own knowledge base instead of the user's. Discovered while dogfooding kbexplorer on the CLI repo itself.
nodes.rawContent: Until this is fixed, `kbexplorer dev` in a vendored install renders the template's own knowledge base instead of the user's. Discovered while dogfooding kbexplorer on the CLI repo itself.
nodes.title: Impact

nodes.content:
In a host repo using kbexplorer init --vendor (so .kbexplorer/ lives one level deep inside the host, not as a git submodule):

node .kbexplorer/scripts/generate-manifest.js

writes a manifest containing the template's stock content (37 files starting with content/app-shell.md, README # kbexplorer-template) rather than the host repo's authored content.
nodes.rawContent:
In a host repo using `kbexplorer init --vendor` (so `.kbexplorer/` lives one level deep inside the host, not as a git submodule):

`
node .kbexplorer/scripts/generate-manifest.js
`

writes a manifest containing the **template's stock content** (37 files starting with `content/app-shell.md`, README `# kbexplorer-template`) rather than the host repo's authored content.
nodes.title: Repro

nodes.content:
At the top of the script:

js const hostRoot = process.env.VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT ? resolve(process.env.VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT) : detectHostRoot();

Falls back to existing behavior for standalone use; honors the explicit env var when the CLI provides it.
nodes.rawContent:
At the top of the script:

`js
const hostRoot = process.env.VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT
  ? resolve(process.env.VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT)
  : detectHostRoot();
`

Falls back to existing behavior for standalone use; honors the explicit env var when the CLI provides it.

nodes.title: Epic: Work-graph vocabulary — teams, workstreams, priorities, releases, people

nodes.content: Drop team.yaml / workstream.yaml / release data into a repo and the graph grows an organizational layer: a workstream node links to its priority, its team, its active PRs and issues, its releases; a person node aggregates their authored/assigned work. Resource-first navigation works across it (click a teammate → their workstream → its open PRs).
nodes.rawContent: Drop `team.yaml` / `workstream.yaml` / release data into a repo and the graph grows an organizational layer: a workstream node links to its priority, its team, its active PRs and issues, its releases; a person node aggregates their authored/assigned work. Resource-first navigation works across it (click a teammate → their workstream → its open PRs).
nodes.title: Outcome

nodes.content:
1. Work-graph entity schema — YAML descriptor shapes for team, workstream, priority, person, system-of-record in the content-model engine, with derived edges (member-of, owns, prioritized-as, tracked-in).
  2. Release nodes — ingestion in kbexplorer-cli (gh release list → manifest) + release node type + edges to PRs/tags here.
  3. Person nodes — promote people from author/assignee strings to first-class nodes aggregating their active work, optionally enriched by the existing OrgChart provider.

Design constraint: schema-first. The descriptor shapes must be reviewable by humans, enforceable in the host repo, and stable across template upgrades (coordinate with kbexplorer-cli#42 capability/protocol work).
nodes.rawContent:
1. **Work-graph entity schema** — YAML descriptor shapes for `team`, `workstream`, `priority`, `person`, `system-of-record` in the content-model engine, with derived edges (member-of, owns, prioritized-as, tracked-in).
2. **Release nodes** — ingestion in kbexplorer-cli (`gh release list` → manifest) + release node type + edges to PRs/tags here.
3. **Person nodes** — promote people from author/assignee strings to first-class nodes aggregating their active work, optionally enriched by the existing OrgChart provider.

Design constraint: schema-first. The descriptor shapes must be reviewable by humans, enforceable in the host repo, and stable across template upgrades (coordinate with kbexplorer-cli#42 capability/protocol work).
nodes.title: Scope (sub-issues)

nodes.content:
The target deployment is a work repository where people need sensemaking over active PRs, work items, releases, workstreams, priorities, and what coworkers are doing. Issues/PRs/commits/branches already ingest, but the organizational layer — the thing that turns repo activity into a navigable map of work — has no vocabulary: no team, workstream, priority, release, person, or system-of-record node types.

The F2 content-model pipeline (schema-driven YAML/JSON entity files under content-model/, Epic #147) is exactly the right substrate. The host work repo will enforce consistency with YAML descriptor files; those descriptors ARE the contract this epic defines.

nodes.title: Search: build-time index + HUD search button + Ctrl-K palette

nodes.content:
• Index: built into the manifest (or a sibling search-index.json) at generate/build time — id, title, type, cluster, headings, body text (tokenized/trimmed). Runtime mode falls back to indexing loaded nodes in-memory. Use a tiny client lib (minisearch or comparable, license-compatible) or hand-rolled inverted index — justify the choice in the PR.
  • UI: a search button in the HUD + global Ctrl-K (and /) command palette: type → ranked results (title match > heading > body) with type/cluster badges → Enter navigates to the node in reading view; arrow keys navigate results. Fluent v9 components, all three themes, keyboard-trap-free, accessible (combobox/listbox semantics).
  • Works in both local-manifest and runtime-GitHub modes.
  • E2E coverage (Playwright) for open-search→type→navigate, plus unit tests for ranking.
  • Result cap + perf budget: index build adds <2s to build; palette opens <100ms on a 500-node graph.

nodes.title: Epic: Standard of beauty — agentic design review + experiential quality bar

nodes.content:
1. Canonical screenshot capture — reproducible script capturing the agreed surface set (all views × all themes × key states) for review input.
  2. BEAUTY.md — the standard — the written bar: principles, per-surface criteria, scoring rubric, and the review protocol. Authored from an actual frontier-model design review of the captured surfaces, not invented in the abstract.
  3. Remediation wave 1 — issues filed from the first assessment, worked through the normal pipeline.

The standard then becomes a recurring gate: future UI PRs cite it, and periodic re-assessment keeps drift visible.

1. **Canonical screenshot capture** — reproducible script capturing the agreed surface set (all views × all themes × key states) for review input.
2. **BEAUTY.md — the standard** — the written bar: principles, per-surface criteria, scoring rubric, and the review protocol. Authored from an actual frontier-model design review of the captured surfaces, not invented in the abstract.
3. **Remediation wave 1** — issues filed from the first assessment, worked through the normal pipeline.

The standard then becomes a recurring gate: future UI PRs cite it, and periodic re-assessment keeps drift visible.
nodes.title: Scope (sub-issues)

nodes.content:
kbexplorer's structural quality has gates (graph validation, assessment scoring, link health). Its experiential quality has none — nothing assesses whether the thing is beautiful: typography rhythm, color and contrast across themes, motion, graph readability, information hierarchy, the feel of moving resource-to-resource. For a sensemaking tool, beauty is not cosmetic; it is load-bearing — visual clarity IS comprehension.

This epic establishes a standard of beauty: an explicit, opinionated quality bar, an agentic review process that assesses the real rendered product against it (screenshots, not source), and a stream of driven improvements.

nodes.title: Plan

nodes.content:
Dependabot alert #7 (moderate severity) flags uuid@13.0.0 in package-lock.json — GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq / CVE-2026-41907: missing buffer bounds check in v3()/v5()/v6() when a caller-provided buf is passed, allowing silent partial writes (CWE-787).

uuid is a transitive (peer) dependency of vis-data/vis-network. First patched version: 13.0.1, which is within the existing ^13.0.0 peer range, so this is a lockfile-only bump.

nodes.title: Epic: Comprehensive testing system — DTU spine across CLI, app, and visual surfaces

nodes.content:
1. CLI ↔ DTU seam [cli] — configurable GitHub API base/auth so the CLI fetches from the Gitea adapter (hermetic) AND a GHE host (real enterprise). Keystone; unblocks the dress rehearsal (cli #56) and the real deployment.
  2. Full-loop deployment scenario — actor mutates twin → CLI regenerates manifest from twin → app renders it → verify reflects the mutation. The end-to-end the real deployment IS.
  3. Work-graph DTU scenarios — actor edits team.yaml/workstream.yaml or cuts a release → app reflects the new team/release node on refresh (extends issue-lifecycle/pr-and-merge to the org layer shipped in #232).
  4. Agent-runtime twin [cli] — deterministic fake agent CLI so derive/generate fuzzy paths run hermetically in full-pipeline tests, not just unit injection.
  5. MCP server twins [cli] — fake ADO board + SharePoint-docs MCP servers so MCP-preflight + derive against work-item/doc sources are exercised hermetically (the work-repo deployment's real dependencies).
  6. Visual-regression gate — wire capture-review + BEAUTY.md into a baseline-diff check (per theme × surface), tied to twin states; catch visual regressions.
  7. TESTING.md — the pyramid + CI orchestration — formalize what runs on PR (unit + static-twin fast gate) vs nightly (live DTU + full-loop + visual) vs exploratory; codify the holdout discipline across all twins.
  8. Exploratory-agent harness — formalize the playbook: a scheduled/triggerable job that launches agent sessions against a running DTU to probe edge cases and open spec PRs (human-reviewed; assertions in specs, never in twins).

CLI-side layers (1, 4, 5) are tracked as issues in anokye-labs/kbexplorer-cli and linked here.

nodes.title: The matrix (service × surface)

nodes.content:
The DTU foundation is live on main: a static GitHub fixture twin (twins/github/, the fast PR gate) and a stateful Gitea live twin (twins/gitea/, Podman + GitHub→Gitea proxy on VITE_GH_API_BASE, scripted actors, nightly). DTU.md states the ambition: local behavioral clones of every external service, with the holdout rule (specs are the holdout set; never code to them).

Today that spine only validates the app (browser, remote mode). The CLI pipeline (init/generate/derive/manifest/build) shells out to gh directly and is tested only by unit injection + the static mock — never against the live, mutating twin. There is no full-loop test (twin mutates → CLI regenerates → app renders → verify), and the project's other external dependencies — agent runtimes (copilot/claude) and MCP servers (ADO, SharePoint) — have no twins at all, despite being the backbone of the local-first regeneration the work-repo deployment depends on.

Surfaced by the work-graph DTU scenarios (#256 / PR #264).

loadRemoteKnowledgeBase() (src/engine/remote-loader.ts) registers new ContentModelProvider(null) — a no-op — so in remote/runtime mode the content-model (work-graph vocabulary: team/workstream/priority/person/system-of-record from #232) is not fetched or rendered. Those nodes only appear in local-manifest mode (the CLI writes them into the manifest).

Impact: a runtime-mode deployment (app fetching live from GitHub in-browser, no CLI-built manifest) shows issues/PRs/releases but NOT the organizational layer. Two .fixme specs in e2e/gitea/workgraph-mutations.spec.ts document this and can be un-fixme'd when the remote fetch path lands.

Fix: implement a remote content-model fetch (read content-model/ files from the repo via the GitHub API / adapter) and pass a populated ContentModelProvider in the remote loader, mirroring the local loader. Relates to the work-graph epic #232.

Created: Jun 13, 2026 · Updated: Jun 13, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

Gap surfaced while writing TESTING.md (#258).

Layer 4 of the test pyramid — the full-loop scenario (e2e/full-loop/actor-regen-render.spec.ts, run via npm run test:e2e:full-loop / playwright.full-loop.config.ts) — currently runs only manually/locally. No scheduled workflow invokes it:

  • dtu-gitea.yml (nightly 04:30 UTC) runs only npm run test:e2e:gitea (layer 3).
  • visual-regression.yml and explore-dtu.yml cover layers 5 and 6.

So the full-loop never executes in CI, and regressions in the actor→twin→CLI-regen→app-render→verify path would not be caught nightly.

Options

  1. Extend dtu-gitea.yml to also run npm run test:e2e:full-loop after the gitea suite (shares the Podman bringup; cheapest).
  2. Add a dedicated nightly workflow for the full-loop.

Option 1 is likely simplest since the substrate/bringup overlaps. Note the full-loop's default substrate is static (FULL_LOOP_SUBSTRATE=static); the live-Gitea substrate is still deferred, so wiring it nightly may also be a good moment to wire the gitea substrate.

TESTING.md documents this as "tracked separately" and points here.

Part of the testing system established in epic #254.

nodes.title: Replace GitHub API with local data for self-exploration

nodes.content:
• npm run dev loads with zero GitHub API calls in local mode

  • Comprehensive unit and scenario tests pass

nodes.title: Acceptance Criteria

nodes.content: kbexplorer fetches ALL content via GitHub API at runtime — authored markdown, file tree, README, issues, PRs, commits, and config.yaml. This causes rate limiting (60 req/hr unauthenticated) and is wasteful for self-exploration where content is on disk.
nodes.rawContent: kbexplorer fetches ALL content via GitHub API at runtime — authored markdown, file tree, README, issues, PRs, commits, and config.yaml. This causes rate limiting (60 req/hr unauthenticated) and is wasteful for self-exploration where content is on disk.
nodes.title: Problem

nodes.content:
A pre-build script generates a single src/generated/repo-manifest.json containing:

  • Authored content: markdown files from content/ read from disk
  • Config: config.yaml parsed from disk
  • File tree: local file system walk
  • README: read from disk
  • Issues, PRs, commits: fetched via gh CLI at build time (best-effort)

The app imports this manifest in local mode — zero API calls at runtime. Remote mode (GitHub API) is preserved for deployed instances exploring other repos.

A pre-build script generates a single `src/generated/repo-manifest.json` containing:

- **Config**: `config.yaml` parsed from disk
- **File tree**: local file system walk
- **README**: read from disk
- **Issues, PRs, commits**: fetched via `gh` CLI at build time (best-effort)

The app imports this manifest in local mode — zero API calls at runtime. Remote mode (GitHub API) is preserved for deployed instances exploring other repos.

nodes.title: Epic: Decouple kbexplorer subsystems & enable pluggable providers/representations

nodes.content:
• Shared contracts live in a separate repo/package @anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core.
  • Affordances are per-retrieval and situational (see §4A of the plan): a source declares a possible universe; each retrieved resource carries the affordances allowed now + hypermedia links. Staging area is a first-class linked resource. Git ≠ GitHub.
  • Provider loading is local-ES-module-first, then 3rd-party npm.
  • llm-context representation is neighbor-anchored & navigable — never the whole graph.
  • Each phase keeps graph output byte-identical until a seam is intentionally flipped.
nodes.rawContent:
- Shared contracts live in a **separate repo/package** `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core`.
- **Affordances are per-*retrieval* and situational** (see §4A of the plan): a source
  declares a possible universe; each retrieved resource carries the affordances allowed
  *now* + hypermedia links. Staging area is a first-class linked resource. **Git ≠ GitHub.**
- Provider loading is **local-ES-module-first**, then 3rd-party npm.
- `llm-context` representation is **neighbor-anchored & navigable** — never the whole graph.
- Each phase keeps graph output **byte-identical** until a seam is intentionally flipped.

nodes.title: Success definition

nodes.content: Today the three subsystems — system-of-record + providers, the resource-graph-engine, and the representation/rendering subsystem — are entangled: two fat loaders duplicate ~150 lines of post-processing, there is no first-class system-of-record abstraction, 3rd-party providers cannot actually load (hardcoded plugin switch), representation styling is baked into core data types, and the SPA is the only output format. Target: a clean 4-layer pipeline — Sources → Providers → Engine (pure KBGraph) → Representation registry — backed by a shared @anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core contracts package, so authors can bring their own local or 3rd-party providers, sources, and representations without forking core.

registry** — backed by a shared `@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core` contracts package, so
authors can bring their own local or 3rd-party providers, sources, and representations
without forking core.

nodes.title: Requirements

nodes.content:
• Walks local file system → produces GHTreeItem-compatible tree (filters dotfiles/node_modules/dist)
  • Reads README.md from disk
  • Reads content/*.md files → embeds raw markdown keyed by path
  • Reads config.yaml → parses and embeds
  • Fetches issues via gh issue list --json ... --state all --limit 200 (best-effort)
  • Fetches PRs via gh pr list --json ... --state all --limit 200 (best-effort)
  • Fetches commits via git log or gh api (best-effort, last 50)
  • Host-aware: detects submodule mode and reads from host repo root
nodes.rawContent:
- Walks local file system → produces GHTreeItem-compatible tree (filters dotfiles/node_modules/dist)
- Reads `README.md` from disk
- Reads `content/*.md` files → embeds raw markdown keyed by path
- Reads `config.yaml` → parses and embeds
- Fetches issues via `gh issue list --json ... --state all --limit 200` (best-effort)
- Fetches PRs via `gh pr list --json ... --state all --limit 200` (best-effort)
- Fetches commits via `git log` or `gh api` (best-effort, last 50)
- Host-aware: detects submodule mode and reads from host repo root

nodes.title: Feature: Phase 4 — Source abstraction with per-retrieval situational affordances

nodes.content:
One loadKnowledgeBase(source, config) replaces both loaders; goldens byte-identical; a staged file resource carries a staging-area link.

Blocked by: F3.
nodes.rawContent:
One `loadKnowledgeBase(source, config)` replaces both loaders; goldens byte-identical; a
staged file resource carries a `staging-area` link.

**Blocked by:** F3.
nodes.title: Acceptance

nodes.content: Source/Resource/Affordance/Link impls, ManifestSource + GitHubApiSource, provider refactor, single loadKnowledgeBase. Out: write/stage mutations beyond the contract + staging-area linking (kept minimal/read-first).
nodes.rawContent:
`Source`/`Resource`/`Affordance`/`Link` impls, `ManifestSource` + `GitHubApiSource`,
provider refactor, single `loadKnowledgeBase`. Out: write/stage *mutations* beyond the
contract + staging-area linking (kept minimal/read-first).
nodes.title: Scope

nodes.content: Introduce the Source abstraction (§4A): a source declares a possible universe of affordances per kind, but each retrieved resource carries the affordances allowed now plus hypermedia links. Staging area is a first-class linked resource. Git ≠ GitHub — GitHubApiSource is a composite exposing Git resources (file/tree/commit/ staging-area) and GitHub resources (issue/pull-request/release). Refactor providers to consume a Source, and collapse the two loaders into one loadKnowledgeBase(source, config).
nodes.rawContent:
Introduce the `Source` abstraction (§4A): a source declares a *possible universe* of
affordances per kind, but each **retrieved resource carries the affordances allowed *now***
plus hypermedia `links`. Staging area is a first-class linked resource. **Git ≠ GitHub** —
`GitHubApiSource` is a composite exposing Git resources (`file`/`tree`/`commit`/
`staging-area`) and GitHub resources (`issue`/`pull-request`/`release`). Refactor providers
to consume a `Source`, and collapse the two loaders into one `loadKnowledgeBase(source, config)`.
nodes.title: What

nodes.content: No first-class system-of-record today; this is what makes "bring your own SoR" possible and unifies build-time vs runtime wiring.
nodes.rawContent:
No first-class system-of-record today; this is what makes "bring your own SoR" possible
and unifies build-time vs runtime wiring.

nodes.title: Epic: Semantic search companion module (kbexplorer-search)

nodes.content:
• Separate @anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search npm package in a new repo.
  • Consumes KBNode/KBGraph/KBConfig types from kbexplorer-core (or inlined initially until kbexplorer-core is published).

  • FAISS (via faiss-node or similar) as the default runtime index, but the design does not depend solely on a native binary index as the only source of truth.
  • Phased delivery: extraction → embedding → artifacts → query engine → CLI → service.

nodes.title: Success definition

nodes.content:
kbexplorer defines a structured knowledge graph: authored markdown nodes, frontmatter metadata, clusters, hierarchy, relationships, and source-aware content. This Epic creates a companion @anokye-labs/kbexplorer-search module that understands that model and turns it into a semantic search corpus — without making the visual graph app or the core CLI responsible for vector-search infrastructure.

The module has two complementary roles:

  1. Index production — reads the kbexplorer content model, derives searchable units from the graph (SearchUnits), generates embeddings via a pluggable provider, and writes checked-in search artifacts (embeddings, index metadata, node-to-vector mappings). These artifacts become part of the repository — they travel with branches, PRs, reviews, releases, and deployments.

  2. Index consumption — loads the checked-in artifacts, builds an efficient vector index (FAISS or similar), embeds incoming queries using the same configured model, and returns kbexplorer-native results: node IDs, titles, paths, clusters, snippets, scores, and graph-aware context.

The repository owns the semantic search corpus; the service only provides query execution. Embeddings and mapping files are durable, reviewable build outputs tied to the exact version of the kbexplorer graph.

The module has two complementary roles:

   These artifacts become part of the repository — they travel with branches, PRs, reviews,
   releases, and deployments.

2. **Index consumption** — loads the checked-in artifacts, builds an efficient vector index
   (FAISS or similar), embeds incoming queries using the same configured model, and returns

The repository owns the semantic search corpus; the service only provides query execution.
Embeddings and mapping files are durable, reviewable build outputs tied to the exact
version of the kbexplorer graph.
nodes.title: What

nodes.content:
Search results should be graph-aware — they know node identity, cluster membership, hierarchy, authored connections, source citations, and page structure. A query for "how does audit validation work?" should return the relevant kbexplorer node, its relationship to nearby concepts, and enough metadata to place the result back into the graph. This makes semantic search feel native to kbexplorer rather than bolted on.

The design also fits the development workflow: a contributor changes content, runs the search index builder, commits both content and updated search artifacts. CI verifies artifact freshness. A hosted service deploys directly from repository state.

nodes.title: Evidence-based completion criteria

nodes.content:
Define and export the core type contracts in src/types.ts:

interface SearchUnit {
  nodeId: string;           // KBNode.id
  chunkIndex: number;       // 0 for single-chunk nodes
  text: string;             // searchable text content
  title: string;            // node title
  cluster: string;          // cluster id
  path?: string;            // source file path
  parentId?: string;        // hierarchy parent
  entityType?: string;      // structured node type
  identity?: string;        // canonical URN
  connections: string[];    // connected node IDs
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>; // extensible
}

interface EmbeddingVector {
  unitId: string;           // `${nodeId}#${chunkIndex}`
  vector: number[];         // embedding values
  model: string;            // model that produced this
  dimensions: number;
}

interface EmbeddingArtifact {
  version: number;
  generatedFrom: string;    // content hash of source graph
  model: string;
  dimensions: number;
  units: SearchUnit[];
  vectors: EmbeddingVector[];
}

interface SearchResult {
  nodeId: string;
  title: string;
  cluster: string;
  score: number;            // cosine similarity
  snippet: string;          // relevant text excerpt
  chunkIndex: number;
  path?: string;
  parentId?: string;
  identity?: string;
  entityType?: string;
  connections: string[];
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
}

interface SearchConfig {
  embedding: {
    provider: string;       // 'openai' | 'local' | 'custom'
    model: string;          // e.g. 'text-embedding-3-small'
    dimensions?: number;
    batchSize?: number;
  };
  artifacts: {
    dir: string;            // output directory for artifacts
  };
  chunking?: {
    maxTokens?: number;
    overlap?: number;
  };
}

interface EmbeddingProvider {
  name: string;
  embed(texts: string[]): Promise<number[][]>;
  dimensions: number;
}

Also inline a minimal subset of kbexplorer types (KBNode, KBEdge, KBGraph, Cluster, Connection) in src/kbexplorer-types.ts with a TODO to switch to @anokye-labs/kbexplorer-core when published.

nodes.title: Feature: Phase 3 — Artifact serialization, checked-in format, and drift gate

nodes.content:
• Write + read round-trip produces byte-identical artifacts.
  • --check detects when content changed but artifacts are stale.
  • --check passes when artifacts are fresh.

Blocked by: F2 (needs embedding generation to produce the artifacts).
nodes.rawContent:
- Write + read round-trip produces byte-identical artifacts.
- `--check` detects when content changed but artifacts are stale.
- `--check` passes when artifacts are fresh.

**Blocked by:** F2 (needs embedding generation to produce the artifacts).
nodes.title: Acceptance

nodes.content:
• Artifact file format: search-artifacts/ directory containing:
    • index-meta.json: version, model, dimensions, unit count, content hash.
    • units.json: SearchUnit array (no vectors — readable, reviewable).
    • vectors.json: EmbeddingVector array (or a binary format for large indexes).
  • Deterministic serialization: sorted keys, stable array order, no timestamps.
  • Drift detection: --check flag that compares committed artifacts against a fresh extraction (without calling the embedding API) and exits non-zero on mismatch.
  • Content-hash computation for the source graph (so artifacts know what they were built from).
nodes.rawContent:
- Artifact file format: `search-artifacts/` directory containing:
  - `index-meta.json`: version, model, dimensions, unit count, content hash.
  - `units.json`: SearchUnit array (no vectors — readable, reviewable).
  - `vectors.json`: EmbeddingVector array (or a binary format for large indexes).
- Deterministic serialization: sorted keys, stable array order, no timestamps.
- Drift detection: `--check` flag that compares committed artifacts against a fresh
  extraction (without calling the embedding API) and exits non-zero on mismatch.
- Content-hash computation for the source graph (so artifacts know what they were built from).
nodes.title: Scope

nodes.content: Define the on-disk artifact format for checked-in search state, implement deterministic serialization, and provide a CI-grade drift detection gate.

nodes.content: The Related panel should rank by edge weight × relevance, not just neighbor degree. A derived_from edge (weight 5.0) should rank higher than a mentions edge (weight 0.5), regardless of the target node's degree.

nodes.title: Expected

nodes.content:
The Related panel in the HUD shows the top 8 neighbors sorted by degree (connection count). This pushes out file nodes and other low-degree nodes, even when they have strong typed edges to the current node.

For example, content-pipeline has a derived_from edge (weight 3.0) to its source file file-content/content-pipeline.md and a references edge (weight 2.0) to file-src/engine/parser.ts — but neither appears in the Related panel because authored nodes with more connections rank higher by raw degree.

nodes.title: Migration Path

nodes.content: vis-network struggles with our current graph size (~150+ nodes, ~250+ edges). Layout stabilization is slow, rendering is jittery, and we're not yet at the scale the provider system will produce. The graph provider architecture will generate 1000+ nodes with 5000+ edges.
nodes.rawContent: vis-network struggles with our current graph size (~150+ nodes, ~250+ edges). Layout stabilization is slow, rendering is jittery, and we're not yet at the scale the provider system will produce. The graph provider architecture will generate 1000+ nodes with 5000+ edges.
nodes.title: Problem

nodes.content: Evaluate Sigma.js + Graphology first — it matches our existing ForceAtlas2 layout, has WebGL rendering, supports custom node programs, and the Graphology data structure aligns well with our typed edge model. If custom node rendering is too limited, fall back to react-force-graph.
nodes.rawContent: Evaluate **Sigma.js + Graphology** first — it matches our existing ForceAtlas2 layout, has WebGL rendering, supports custom node programs, and the Graphology data structure aligns well with our typed edge model. If custom node rendering is too limited, fall back to **react-force-graph**.

nodes.title: Research Summary

nodes.content:
Sigma.js + Graphology

  • Best 2D WebGL option for 10k+ nodes
  • Graphology handles graph data structure, Sigma renders
  • Custom node programs (WebGL shaders) for shapes
  • Force-directed via ForceAtlas2 (same algorithm we use now)
  • Active v3 with modern API

react-force-graph

  • Native React component, WebGL via Three.js
  • 2D and 3D modes
  • Best for React integration
  • Force-directed only (d3-force)
  • Comprehensive styling

Cosmos

  • Full GPU simulation AND rendering
  • Fastest at extreme scale
  • Limited styling (no custom node shapes yet)
  • Newest, least proven
nodes.rawContent:
### Sigma.js + Graphology
- Best 2D WebGL option for 10k+ nodes
- Graphology handles graph data structure, Sigma renders
- Custom node programs (WebGL shaders) for shapes
- Force-directed via ForceAtlas2 (same algorithm we use now)
- Active v3 with modern API

### react-force-graph
- Native React component, WebGL via Three.js
- 2D and 3D modes
- Best for React integration
- Force-directed only (d3-force)
- Comprehensive styling

### Cosmos
- Full GPU simulation AND rendering
- Fastest at extreme scale
- Limited styling (no custom node shapes yet)
- Newest, least proven

Created: Apr 4, 2026 · Updated: Apr 10, 2026

[View on GitHub ↗](https://github.com/anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template/issues/9)

---

## Visual Identity System

### Icon Rendering
- Fluent icons sourced from `@fluentui/react-icons`, colored with their cluster color (not monochrome)
- Icons are drawn as SVG data URIs inside canvas shapes, with paths defined in `ICON_PATHS` (`nodeRenderer.ts`)

### Custom Node Shapes
- vis-network nodes use custom shapes via `ctxRenderer`: circles, rounded squares, and rounded rectangles
- Opaque node backgrounds prevent edges from showing through the node fill
- Disconnected nodes display a red **!** badge to flag orphan state

### Component Architecture
- `NodeVisual` component accepts a `clusterColor` prop for consistent color theming
- The 7 cluster surfaces still apply for UI chrome, but graph nodes bypass `NodeVisual` and use the custom canvas renderer directly

  • Improved source locations and error display in compiler diagnostics. (@​nathanmarks in #35348, @​josephsavona in #34963)

7.0.1

  • Disallowed passing inline useEffectEvent values as JSX props to guard against accidental propagation. (#34820 by @​jf-eirinha)
  • Switch to export = so eslint-plugin-react-hooks emits correct types for consumers in Node16 ESM projects. (#34949 by @​karlhorky)
  • Tightened the typing of configs.flat so the configs export is always defined. (#34950 by @​poteto)
  • Fix named import runtime errors. (#34951, #34953 by @​karlhorky)

7.0.0

This release slims down presets to just 2 configurations (recommended and recommended-latest), and all compiler rules are enabled by default.

  • Breaking: Removed recommended-latest-legacy and flat/recommended configs. The plugin now provides recommended (legacy and flat configs with all recommended rules), and recommended-latest (legacy and flat configs with all recommended rules plus new bleeding edge experimental compiler rules). (@​poteto in #34757)

6.1.1

Note: 6.1.0 accidentally allowed use of recommended without flat config, causing errors when used with ESLint v9's defineConfig() helper. This has been fixed in 6.1.1.

  • Fix recommended config for flat config compatibility. The recommended config has been converted to flat config format. Non-flat config users should use recommended-legacy instead. (@​poteto in #34700)
  • Add recommended-latest and recommended-latest-legacy configs that include React Compiler rules. (@​poteto in #34675)
  • Remove unused NoUnusedOptOutDirectives rule. (@​poteto in #34703)
  • Remove hermes-parser and dependency. (@​poteto in #34719)
  • Remove @babel/plugin-proposal-private-methods dependency. (@​ArnaudBarre and @​josephsavona in #34715)
  • Update for Zod v3/v4 compatibility. (@​kolian and @​josephsavona in #34717)

6.1.0

Note: Version 6.0.0 was mistakenly released and immediately deprecated and untagged on npm. This is the first official 6.x major release and includes breaking changes.

  • Breaking: Require Node.js 18 or newer. (@​michaelfaith in #32458)
  • Breaking: Flat config is now the default recommended preset. Legacy config moved to recommended-legacy. (@​michaelfaith in #32457)
  • New Violations: Disallow calling use within try/catch blocks. (@​poteto in #34040)

🔴 CLOSED · PR #125

Created: Apr 19, 2026 · Updated: Apr 19, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

Problem

The sidebar resize grip bars were rendering on the grey border band instead of inside the dark sidebar content area.

Root Cause

The handle was positioned with
ight: 2px\ from the parent's edge. The parent (expandedContent) has no border — the 6px border lives on the grandparent (hudContainer). So
ight: 2\ placed the bars right at the visual border boundary.

Fix

  • Widened handle hit zone to 32px (was 16px) for easier grabbing
  • Changed justifyContent to \ lex-start/\ lex-end\ based on dock direction
  • Added 10px margin to push bars clearly into the dark sidebar area
  • Works correctly for both left and right dock positions

Verification

Closeup screenshots confirm bars are clearly inside the dark sidebar area, separated from the grey border, for both left and right dock positions.

This feature release contains a couple of notable changes:

  • There is a new configuration option show_patched_versions which will add a column to the output, showing the fix version of each vulnerable dependency. Thanks @​felickz!

Updates react-router from 7.14.2 to 7.16.0

Release notes

Sourced from react-router's releases.

v7.16.0

See the changelog for release notes: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v7160

v7.15.1

See the changelog for release notes: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v7151

v7.15.0

See the changelog for release notes: https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v7150

Changelog

Sourced from react-router's changelog.

v7.16.0

Minor Changes

  • Stabilize future.unstable_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests as future.v8_trailingSlashAwareDataRequests (#15098)

Patch Changes

  • Disable manifest path when lazy route dicovery is disabled (#15068)

  • Fix browser URL creation to use the configured history window instead of the global window. (#15066)

    • Pass the history/router window through to createBrowserURLImpl so custom window contexts keep the correct URL origin.

  • Fix useNavigation() return type to preserve discriminated union across navigation states (#15095)

  • Widen MetaDescriptor script:ld+json type from LdJsonObject to LdJsonObject | LdJsonObject[] to permit multiple JSON-LD schemas in a single <script type="application/ld+json"> tag emitted by <Meta /> (#15082)

v7.15.1

Patch Changes

  • Update router to operate on fetcher Maps in an immutable manner to avoid delayed React renders from potentially reading an updated but not yet committed Map. This could result in brief flickers in some fetcher-driven optimistic UI scenarios. (#15028)
  • Fix serverLoader() returning stale SSR data when a client navigation aborts pending hydration before the hydration clientLoader resolves (#15022)
  • Fix RouterProvider onError callback not being called for synchronous initial loader errors in SPA mode (#15039) (#14942)
  • Memoize useFetchers to return a stable identity and only change if fetchers changed (#15028)
  • Internal refactor to consolidate mutation request detection through shared utility (#15033)

Unstable Changes

⚠️ Unstable features are not recommended for production use

  • Add a new unstable_useRouterState() hook that consolidates access to active and pending router states (RFC: #12358) (#15017)

    • Data/Framework/RSC only — throws when used without a data router

    • This should allow you to consolidate usages of the following hooks which will likely be deprecated and removed in a future major version

      • useLocation
      • useSearchParams
      • useParams
      • useMatches
      • useNavigationType
      • useNavigation
      let { active, pending } = unstable_useRouterState();

      // Active is always populated with the current location
active.location; // replaces useLocation()
active.searchParams; // replaces useSearchParams()[0]
active.params; // replaces useParams()
active.matches; // replaces useMatches()
active.type; // replaces useNavigationType()

... (truncated)

  • d71025d Stabilize trailing slash aware data requests (#15098)
  • 6e21b63 fix: keep useNavigation() return type a discriminated union (#15095)
  • 4cde90b Support array of objects for script:ld+json meta descriptor (#15082)
  • dc996ea fix(router): pass configured window to createBrowserURLImpl (#15066)
  • cfb5fb0 Disable manifest handler when lazy route discovery is disabled (#15068)

Created: Jun 9, 2026 · Updated: Jun 9, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

Summary

Brings the repo-setup work onto current main. The original feature/repo-setup branch had diverged into a parallel re-implementation of the app; rather than replay that (which would regress main, the live/deployed branch), this rebases onto main and keeps only the genuinely additive pieces: repository governance files, the dependency bumps, and the kbexplorer KB agent/skill upgrades.

Related Issue

Refs #

Changes

  • Repo governance (from #60, #70, #72): .editorconfig, .env.example, .github/CODEOWNERS, .github/dependabot.yml, .prettierrc.json, CONTRIBUTING.md, PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md, and PR-gating workflows (dependency-review, linked-issue, pr-title). AGENTS.md kept as main's app-dev guide.
  • Dependency bumps (lockfile regenerated): marked 17->18, react/react-dom 19.2.4->19.2.5, react-router-dom 7.14.0->7.14.2, @eslint/js + eslint 9->10, eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.0.1->7.1.1, globals 17.4->17.5, typescript 5.9->6.0, vite 8.0.1->8.0.5.
  • KB agents/skill: kb-architect and kb-writer rewritten from the microsoft/skills deep-wiki plugin (MIT), new kb-researcher agent, new .github/skills/kbexplorer/ skill, ignore .env.kbexplorer.

Excludes the Azure Static Web Apps deploy workflow (this repo deploys via GitHub Pages).

Verification

  • Build/tests run
  • Manual or API verification completed
  • Evidence: Verified against a clean main baseline. npx vite build passes, vitest 176/176, Playwright e2e (chromium) 46/46 including markdown-rendering visual tests (covers the marked major). eslint 10 runs the existing flat config and reports the same pre-existing issues as eslint 9 (no new errors). Pre-existing tsc -b / eslint issues on main are unchanged and not deploy gates.

Checklist

  • Linked issue referenced
  • Documentation updated if needed

Release notes

Sourced from actions/upload-artifact's releases.

v7.0.0

v7 What's new

Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. The action will fail if the glob passed resolves to multiple files. The name parameter is also ignored with this setting. Instead, the name of the artifact will be the name of the uploaded file.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Add proxy integration test by @​Link- in actions/upload-artifact#754
  • Upgrade the module to ESM and bump dependencies by @​danwkennedy in actions/upload-artifact#762
  • Support direct file uploads by @​danwkennedy in actions/upload-artifact#764

New Contributors

🟢 OPEN · PR #146

Created: Jun 10, 2026 · Updated: Jun 10, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

The bug

Vendored/submodule installs render the template's own bundled demo content instead of the host repo's content/. detectHostRoot() never resolves correctly because of two compounding bugs:

  1. Checks pkg.name === 'kbexplorer', but the template's own package.json#name is kbexplorer-template — so the if-branch never executed for any real install.
  2. parentRoot = resolve(kbRoot, '..', '..') goes two levels up from /.kbexplorer, landing in the parent of the host repo.

The fix

  • Accept 'kbexplorer', 'kbexplorer-template', and '@anokye-labs/kbexplorer-template' as template package names.
  • parentRoot = resolve(kbRoot, '..') — one level up, which is the host root.
  • Honor a VITE_KB_HOST_ROOT env override so consumers (kbexplorer-cli) can be explicit instead of relying on filename heuristics.

Verification

  • 176/176 existing tests still pass ( npm test).

  • End-to-end: copied this script into a vendored install of the template inside the kbexplorer-cli repo. Before the fix, the manifest reported Submodule mode: false and rendered 269 demo nodes from the template's own content/. After the fix, it reports:

    [generate-manifest] Submodule mode: true [generate-manifest] Repo: kbexplorer-cli
    [generate-manifest] Content: 23 files

and the explorer renders the host's authored knowledge base correctly.

Feature F1 — Open node-type foundation (JSON-LD nodes + registries)

Foundational feature of Epic #147: turns kbexplorer into an open, data-driven node-type engine. F2 (#149), F3 (#150) and the cli repo's F8 (#18) are blocked-by this surface — the contract is also published as a comment on #148 for early consumption.

All changes are additive and backward-compatible: a node/edge/provider that omits the new fields behaves exactly as before.

What landed

Task Sub-issue Summary
T1.1 #154 KBNode.entityType / jsonld (@context/@id/@type + LD props) / data bag; buildJsonLd() helper (@id reuses identity URN; @type never path-derived).
T1.2 #155 Open DisplayMode (KnownDisplayMode | (string & {}), 'entity' escape hatch); NodeSource gains a clean { type:'structured'; entityType; ref? } variant; node-type registry.
T1.3 #156 Open EdgeType; KBEdge.relation / Connection.relation; 6-relation taxonomy (leads|staffs|reports-to|structural|derived|deprecated) with getEdgeStyle/getEdgeLegendKey/getEdgeWeight; data-driven HUD legend.
T1.4 #157 Viewer registry (src/views/viewers): registerViewer/resolveViewer + mandatory GenericStructuredView fallback; PersonView example.
T1.5 #155 getNodeLayer is now registry-driven via resolveNodeLayer (built-ins pre-registered → byte-identical layer output).
T1.6 #158/#159 ReadingView display:'entity' resolves a viewer; SourceBadge handles structured; CACHE_VERSION 12 → 13; content/node-types.md contract doc; 33 new unit tests.

Design decisions

  • NodeSource opened via a clean structured variant instead of (string & {}), to preserve exhaustive narrowing in SourceBadge/identity. New node types reuse structured + a registry entityType and never edit the core union.
  • Single styling source of truth (getEdgeStyle) shared by the graph renderer and the legend, so they can't drift.
  • No runtime import cycle: types/index.ts imports resolveNodeLayer (value) from the registry, which imports types type-only.
  • Off-by-default demo seam injectDemoEntities() (?demo=entities / localStorage['kbe-demo-entities']) seeds person/team entities + relation edges for e2e evidence without polluting real graphs.

  • ✅ npm test — 209 unit tests passing (33 new: JSON-LD/edge contract, node-type registry, viewer registry incl. SSR render, demo seam).
  • ✅ npx vite build green (default + VITE_KB_LOCAL local build).

  • Repo rules honored: no pixel layout sizing (viewer CSS uses rem/%/tokens; 1px borders only); CACHE_VERSION bumped for the new cached shape.

  1. content-model.md is not present in this repo (likely a sibling-worktree artifact) → sub-issues #154–#159 treated as authoritative, adopting the 6-relation taxonomy + kg:// @id + "@type never from path" rules from the brief.
  2. NodeSource opened via the clean structured variant (narrowing safety).
  3. Added the off-by-default demo seam to produce Playwright evidence.

🟣 MERGED · PR #173

Created: Jun 10, 2026 · Updated: Jun 10, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

Closes #172

What

Hygiene-only changes so the typecheck and lint gates are honestly green on main. No runtime behavior changes.

Before / after

Gate Before After
npx tsc -b 52 errors 0 (exits 0 with the generated manifest present and absent)
npm run lint 40 errors, 1 warning 0 errors (1 pre-existing react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warning retained — see below)
npm test (vitest) green green — 215 passed
npx vite build green green

Changes

  • Test typecheck: added tsconfig.test.json (with @types/node) covering src/**/__tests__/** and excluded __tests__ from tsconfig.app.json. Fixes node:fs / node:path / __dirname errors in the test files.
  • Generated manifest: added an ambient declaration src/generated/repo-manifest.d.ts for the gitignored, prebuild-generated repo-manifest.json, so tsc -b is self-sufficient whether or not the manifest has been generated (TS2307).
  • erasableSyntaxOnly: converted provider constructor parameter properties (private x: T) to explicit field declarations + assignments in authored-provider, files-provider, and work-provider (TS1294). The TS1294 errors were parameter properties, not enums.
  • Unused imports/locals: removed across HUD, HomePageWidgets, IconGallery, HomePage, createGraphNetwork, local-loader, nodemap, providers, remote-loader, and two test files.
  • Griffel type errors: the forbidden borderColor shorthand → accepted border shorthand (same rendered result); numeric width/height (32/80/10) → string values.
  • remote-loader: null → undefined for optional AuthoredProvider args (TS2345); let → const (prefer-const); dropped 3 unused re-exported helpers.
  • work-provider: dropped a gratuitous as any — 'repository' is already a valid DisplayMode.
  • NodeVisual: Object.hasOwn(...) instead of Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty (no-prototype-builtins).
  • eslint: aligned @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars with tsc's noUnusedParameters by ignoring ^_-prefixed args/vars/caught errors (covers the _config / _existingNodes provider params).

Suppressions (justified)

  • 3 × // eslint-disable-next-line react-refresh/only-export-components in NodeVisual.tsx for the co-located non-component exports (FLUENT_ICONS, isFluentIconName, getVisNodeConfig). This is an HMR-only DX rule with no runtime/correctness impact; the proper "fix" would mean carving a ~2,600-entry table and helpers out of a 5,000-line shared node-viewer module — a large, conflict-prone move while F2/F3 are actively editing that surface.
  • 1 retained warning: react-hooks/exhaustive-deps in HUD.tsx is a pre-existing warning (does not fail lint) tied to the single-canvas HUD design; left untouched to avoid a behavior change.

Concurrency

Kept every change minimal and mechanical to limit conflicts with the in-flight F2 (#149) and F3 (#150) branches. Branch is based on the current origin/main (F2/F3 not yet merged); will re-run both gates after any rebase before merge.

- **Griffel type errors:** the forbidden `borderColor` shorthand → accepted `border` shorthand (same rendered result); numeric `width`/`height` (`32`/`80`/`10`) → string values.
- **`remote-loader`:** `null` → `undefined` for optional `AuthoredProvider` args (TS2345); `let` → `const` (`prefer-const`); dropped 3 unused re-exported helpers.
- **`work-provider`:** dropped a gratuitous `as any` — `'repository'` is already a valid `DisplayMode`.
- **`NodeVisual`:** `Object.hasOwn(...)` instead of `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` (`no-prototype-builtins`).
- **eslint:** aligned `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` with tsc's `noUnusedParameters` by ignoring `^_`-prefixed args/vars/caught errors (covers the `_config` / `_existingNodes` provider params).

## Suppressions (justified)
- **3 × `// eslint-disable-next-line react-refresh/only-export-components`** in `NodeVisual.tsx` for the co-located non-component exports (`FLUENT_ICONS`, `isFluentIconName`, `getVisNodeConfig`). This is an HMR-only DX rule with no runtime/correctness impact; the proper "fix" would mean carving a ~2,600-entry table and helpers out of a 5,000-line shared node-viewer module — a large, conflict-prone move while F2/F3 are actively editing that surface.
- **1 retained warning:** `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` in `HUD.tsx` is a pre-existing *warning* (does not fail lint) tied to the single-canvas HUD design; left untouched to avoid a behavior change.

## Concurrency
Kept every change minimal and mechanical to limit conflicts with the in-flight F2 (#149) and F3 (#150) branches. Branch is based on the current `origin/main` (F2/F3 not yet merged); will re-run both gates after any rebase before merge.

T3.1 — Declarative node-map.yaml + heuristic inference (#166)

  • src/engine/node-map.ts: a pure mapper. Declarative rules (glob/shape → @type → field/edge mapping) plus a heuristic shape-inference fallback that maps an unmapped structured file to a sensible JSON-LD node (Workflow, SoftwareApplication, DependabotConfig, ParameterisedConfig, StructuredConfig).
  • Emits nodes via buildJsonLd(); identity URN reused as @id; reversible (full parsed object kept on node.data, reconstructSource() re-serializes).

  • src/engine/providers/structural-provider.ts: discovers workflows, composite Actions, issue/PR templates, issue-template config, CODEOWNERS, dependabot, FUNDING (+ generic config via the node-map), and emits each as a node linked to the single repository (repo-meta) node via a structural relation edge (type:'contains', weight:5).
  • registerStructuralTypes() registers entityTypes (F1 node-type registry) and viewers (viewer registry). dependencies:['work'] so repo-meta exists first. Safe no-op on empty input.

T3.3 — Structural + generic-config viewers (#168)

  • WorkflowView (triggers / jobs / steps) and ActionView (inputs / outputs / runs); generic configs fall back to the mandatory GenericStructuredView.
  • ReadingView gains a scoped "Related structure" panel (only for provider==='structural' nodes) so the .github → repository edges are visible and navigable. No change to other node kinds or to graph data.

Wiring

  • scripts/generate-manifest.js collects .github/** + CODEOWNERS + node-map.yaml (size-capped).
  • local-loader.ts / remote-loader.ts register StructuralProvider (guarded on non-empty input).
  • CACHE_VERSION 13 → 14 (cached-data shape changed). Note: a sibling session (F2 #149) may also bump this — expect a trivial conflict to resolve at merge.
  • No pixel layout sizing in the new CSS (rem/em/tokens; 1px borders only).

Evidence

vitest — 252 pass (was 215 on the F1 base; +37):

  • src/engine/__tests__/node-map.test.ts — 21
  • src/engine/__tests__/providers/structural-provider.test.ts — 14
  • src/engine/__tests__/structural-graph.test.ts — 2 (asserts the workflow → repo-meta edge carries relation:'structural', plus orphan-safe behaviour with no repository node)

npx vite build — green (default + local presets). npm run build/tsc -b/npm run lint remain RED across untouched files on main (Bug #172, out of scope); all new/changed files are type-clean and lint-clean.

Playwright (e2e/structural-nodes.spec.ts, chromium) — 2 pass, on the real local cached-data flow:

  • The .github/workflows/github-pages.yml node renders WorkflowView (triggers push/pull_request/workflow_dispatch; 3 jobs with steps), the Workflow · github-pages.yml SourceBadge, and a "Related structure → kbexplorer-template · configures the repository" link — i.e. a workflow node visibly edged to the repository node. Following the link navigates to #/node/repo-meta.

  • The verified flow is local mode (VITE_KB_LOCAL), where repo-meta exists (WorkProvider with repo metadata). In remote mode repo-meta isn't created, so structural nodes orphan-connect to the graph hub via the existing safe fallback — acceptable and non-breaking.

🟣 MERGED · PR #175

Created: Jun 10, 2026 · Updated: Jun 11, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

Closes #149

Implements F2 — Content-model ingestion pipeline: a schema-driven, 5-pass graph builder that turns a content-model source (schema files + entity files) into typed, JSON-LD-backed KBNodes on top of the merged F1 open node-type foundation (#148).

[!IMPORTANT] The content-model source repo is being sunset and is not in this repo. The schema + entity formats are therefore defined by the fixtures under src/engine/content-model/__tests__/fixtures/content-model/, designed to read the real files when they later land. The pipeline is a safe no-op when no source is detected — existing graph output is byte-identical (215-test baseline stays green).

Sub-issues

  • Closes #160 — T2.1 Schema reader: parses teamops.yaml, schema/{conventions,edges,lifecycle}.yaml, index/context.jsonld. URN bases come from the JSON-LD context only; node kind comes from @type, never the file path; CURIE→URN + org/authority scoping.
  • Closes #161 — T2.2 ContentModelProvider discovery + node emission: walks entity files, detects flat vs nested org layout, builds a (kind,org,id) index, emits JSON-LD nodes via buildJsonLd().
  • Closes #162 — T2.3 Edge resolution: scalar / array / composite / alias FK + derived (shared-target) + deprecated edges; unresolved refs stubbed with diagnostics; every edge typed with a relation.
  • Closes #163 — T2.4 Loader + build-time assembly: provider registered in remote-loader.ts + local-loader.ts; readContentModel() build path in scripts/generate-manifest.js; CACHE_VERSION 13→14.
  • Closes #164 — T2.5 Spine viewers Person + Squad (the original ask): bespoke viewers via the viewer registry; the example PersonView replaced with the real one + new SquadView.
  • Closes #165 — T2.6 Spine viewers Workstream, Mission, Priority, Cycle, Org.

Design highlights

  • Relationships ride on connections. The orchestrator ignores a provider's edges and buildGraph derives edges from each node's connections; the builder attaches typed connections to source nodes (and also returns a directed edges array for unit tests).
  • Reversible nodes. node.data is the verbatim parsed record; the lifecycle band is surfaced on jsonld only; buildJsonLd() writes reserved keys (@context/@id/@type) last so data can't override them. node.id === identity === <URN>.
  • No-op guard. Source is "present" iff teamops.yaml + index/context.jsonld exist; the provider checks this before registering any node types/viewers, so the registries (and layer output) are untouched when absent.
  • Repo rules. Viewers are className-styled / SSR-safe with no pixel sizing; CACHE_VERSION bumped.

Evidence

  • vitest: 255 passed (215 baseline + 40 new) across 22 files — schema-reader.test.ts (10), builder.test.ts (17), content-model-provider.test.ts (3), spine-viewers.test.ts (7), generate-manifest.test.js (+3 readContentModel).
  • npx vite build: green.
  • New/changed files are lint-clean (npm run lint / tsc -b remain pre-existing red on main across untouched files — Bug #172, out of scope).
  • Playwright (local cached-data flow): Person, Squad and Mission nodes render through their bespoke viewers with relationships resolved (verified against a staged content-model/ dir + generate-manifest + VITE_KB_LOCAL build).

Closes #151 Closes #169 Closes #170

Capstone feature validating the new open-node-type system (F1 #148 / F2 #149 / F3 #150) end-to-end, plus two cross-cutting release-readiness items folded in from sibling sessions.

T4.1 — Real-content E2E (#169)

e2e/integration-validation.spec.ts runs on the real local cached-data flow (persisted kbe-demo-entities setting + warmed cache via /#/node/readme), not a clean-state shortcut. Three tests, screenshots captured as evidence under e2e/artifacts/f4-*.png:

  • Person → PersonView — demo-person-ada resolves its bespoke .kb-person-view.
  • Squad → SquadView — demo-squad-orbit resolves its bespoke .kb-squad-view.
  • Workflow → WorkflowView + structural edge — gh-workflow-github-pages-yml renders via .kb-workflow-view AND exposes a navigable structural edge to the repo-meta repository node.

The demo-entities seam is layered on the real build (it's how Person/Squad reach the browser without polluting the template's default graph or risking URN routing). The F2 production pipeline itself is proven at the engine level by the idempotency + derived-artifact + existing content-model-provider tests.

T4.2 — Full-pipeline regression / drift (#170)

  • src/engine/__tests__/pipeline-idempotency.test.ts — content-model build and provider orchestration are byte-identical across re-runs (the "do I need to re-run after source changes?" guarantee), plus safe-no-op invariants: absent content-model and absent .github leave existing graph output unchanged.
  • scripts/check-manifest-drift.js (npm run validate:drift) — asserts the source-derived manifest is deterministic and in sync with committed sources (compares only deterministic source-derived fields; excludes volatile issue/PR/commit/timestamp data). Wired into CI after manifest generation.

Cross-repo derived-artifact proof (F8 gap)

Committed *.jsonld fixtures (KBNode mirror — entityType+jsonld+data, kg:// identity URNs, reports-to/leads relations) + src/engine/__tests__/derived-artifact-render.test.ts proving the engine consumes a cli-emitted derived artifact end-to-end and resolves it to a structured node + bespoke viewer.

CI concurrency hardening (F3 release-readiness infra)

.github/workflows/github-pages.yml previously used one global pages concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: true, so PR test runs cancelled every in-flight run (killing siblings' e2e mid-run). Now scoped per-ref:

concurrency:
  group: pages-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

PR runs only supersede older runs of the same PR; pushes to main (the only ref that deploys) get a distinct group and are never cancelled mid-deploy — preserving the Pages deploy contract.

Gates

All green locally: npx tsc -b = 0, npm run lint = 0 errors, npm test (vitest) = 304 passed, npx vite build = 0, Playwright chromium = 54 passed. CACHE_VERSION unchanged (no cached-shape change).

🟣 MERGED · PR #177

Created: Jun 11, 2026 · Updated: Jun 11, 2026

View on GitHub ↗

Closes #178.

Cherry-picks 9a2163b onto main.

Adds a repo-local skill under .agents/skills/wbs-builder/ that materializes an Epic → Feature → Task work-breakdown structure as real GitHub issues via the GraphQL API, with native issue types, parent/child sub-issues, and blocked-by dependency edges, before any implementation begins.

  • scripts/create-wbs.mjs: resumable runner (discover|create|sub|deps|all, --dry-run/--data/--map). Discovers repository and org-scoped issue-type IDs at runtime by name per owner/repo; no hardcoded node IDs. Journals key→id/number/url to wbs-map.json for resume.
  • scripts/wbs-data.example.mjs: template WBS definition (REPOS, KIND_TYPE_NAMES, ITEMS, DEPS) plus the task() body helper.
  • references/wbs-authoring.md: hierarchy + body templates, native-metadata model, GraphQL mechanics, mandatory per-owner ID discovery, and idempotent execution discipline.
  • AGENTS.md: document the skill under a new Skills section.

Review hardening (follow-up commit)

  • gql() now checks res.ok and parses defensively, surfacing concise HTTP/non-JSON errors.
  • Added an upfront validateWbs() so unknown repo/kind, non-string title/body, duplicate keys, and bad parent/DEPS references fail with actionable messages.
  • Sub-issue linking failures are now persisted to wbs-map.json and skipped on re-run until cleared, matching the dependency-edge behavior and the docs.

Created: Jun 11, 2026 · Updated: Jun 11, 2026

Closes #188

Summary

Wires config.theme.default into the initial theme mode resolution. Previously useTheme ignored config.theme.default entirely and always defaulted to 'dark' when no kbe-theme value was stored.

Resolution order is now:

  1. User's explicitly saved kbe-theme (localStorage) — always wins
  2. config.theme.default — applied once config resolves
  3. 'dark' — final fallback

A config default is applied but not persisted (it isn't a user choice), so a later change to config.theme.default can still take effect for users who never picked a theme.

Changes

  • src/hooks/useTheme.ts:
    • Added readStoredRaw() (returns null when nothing valid is stored) and a pure resolveInitialMode(configDefault?) helper.
    • useTheme() now returns a 4th element, applyConfigDefault(configDefault?), which sets the mode to the config default only when no theme is stored.
  • src/App.tsx: Explorer calls applyConfigDefault(config.theme.default) via useEffect once useKnowledgeBase() reaches ready (config is loaded async, after useTheme first initializes).

Did not touch the dark/light/sepia theme definitions or bump CACHE_VERSION (that's T1.3).

Tests

New src/hooks/__tests__/useTheme.test.ts:

  • config.default applies when no stored theme
  • stored theme wins over config.default
  • falls back to dark when no stored theme and no config default
  • ignores an invalid config default and falls back to dark

Validation

  • npm run lint — pass (0 errors; 1 pre-existing unrelated warning in HUD.tsx)
  • npx vitest run — pass (309/309)
  • npm run build — pass
